mainTopic: Moving objects on שבת and יום טוב: טלטול for a purpose (לצורך גופו, לצורך מקומו, מחמה לצל), and when broken pieces and leftover items count as מוקצה
overview: This amud is about moving objects on שבת and יום טוב. First, the גמרא uses the view of בית שמאי to show that the ban on טלטול grows out of the ban on הוצאה. It then shows that רב agrees with רבא: a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור may be moved for its own use (לצורך גופו) or for its spot (לצורך מקומו), but not just to protect it. The stories of רב כהנא's net, רב מרי's cushions, and the palm brooms all test this rule. Next, a new משנה rules that shards of כלים may be moved if they are still useful. רבי יהודה requires that the use be similar to the original one. שמואל's explanation of the משנה is challenged from a ברייתא about burning shards on יום טוב, and it is restated as a dispute over whether shards broken on שבת are מוכן or נולד. The amud ends with rulings on leftover bricks, small shards in different areas, and a broken jug seal. It closes with רב פפא's challenge to the rule about objects thrown into the garbage, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה about carrying a child, a לולב, and a ספר תורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from מסכת ביצה. בית שמאי forbid carrying a child, a לולב, or a ספר תורה into the public domain on יום טוב. בית הלל permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not carry a child, a לולב, or a ספר תורה out to the public domain on יום טוב. בית הלל permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to support a point about moving objects: a מחלוקת between בית שמאי and בית הלל about carrying on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום טוב, the Torah allows הוצאה when it is needed for food. בית הלל say that once הוצאה is allowed for food, it is allowed for other needs too. בית שמאי disagree and forbid carrying things that are not for food, like a child or a לולב. The גמרא wants to use בית שמאי's strict view to learn something about moving objects in general.

keyTerms.meaning: carry out, from one domain to another (the act of הוֹצָאָה)
the palm branch used on סוכות

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'בית שמאי אומרים' are not written here. Still, the first half of the line is בית שמאי's opinion, because it is set against 'ובית הלל מתירין.' Also, this case is about יום טוב, not שבת.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מוֹצִיאִין אֶת הַקָּטָן וְאֶת הַלּוּלָב
phrases.english: One may not carry out a child or a lulav
phrases.notes: This is the opinion of בית שמאי, on יום טוב.

phrases.english: or a Torah scroll to the public domain,
and Beit Hillel permit it.
phrases.notes: בית הלל allow carrying on יום טוב even for needs that are not food.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מוֹצִיאִין אֶת הַקָּטָן וְאֶת הַלּוּלָב וְאֶת סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues an argument from earlier on the daf by quoting a supporting source.
steps.raayaObject: That בית שמאי forbid carrying when it is not for a real (food) need, and so would also forbid moving objects without a purpose.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מסכת ביצה about carrying a child, a לולב, and a ספר תורה on יום טוב.

steps.title: Maybe carrying out and moving are different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. Perhaps בית שמאי only forbid carrying from one domain to another, not simply moving an object around.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that you heard בית שמאי forbid carrying out (הוצאה). Did you hear them forbid moving an object (טלטול)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 1. It says the source only talks about הוצאה, not טלטול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הוצאה means carrying between domains, which is a Torah-level מלאכה. טלטול means moving an object, even inside one domain. That is only a rabbinic restriction. The challenge says you cannot learn a rule about טלטול from a rule about הוצאה, because they may be totally different.

keyTerms.meaning: say, granted (it opens a 'granted X, but Y?' argument)
carrying from one domain to another
moving an object, even without leaving the domain
did you hear? (a challenge to the proof)

phrases.english: Say that you heard them,
Beit Shammai, forbid carrying out,
but did you hear them forbid moving?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר דְּשָׁמְעַתְּ לְהוּ לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי הוֹצָאָה, טִלְטוּל מִי שָׁמְעַתְּ לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof brought in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof only; the rule itself is not rejected.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The source is about הוצאה, while the question is about טלטול. One cannot be learned from the other.

steps.title: Moving is forbidden because of carrying out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the pushback. The rabbinic ban on טלטול exists only because of הוצאה, so whoever forbids one forbids the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't the ban on moving itself there because of carrying out?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the proof from step 1. It explains that טלטול and הוצאה are connected, so the distinction from step 2 does not hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים banned טלטול as a fence, so that people would not come to do הוצאה. Since טלטול is built on הוצאה, if בית שמאי are strict about הוצאה, they are surely strict about טלטול. So the original proof stands.

keyTerms.meaning: is it not because of? (a rhetorical question meaning 'surely it is because of')

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows an important idea: the rabbinic ban on טלטול is a גזירה that grows out of the Torah ban of הוצאה.

phrases.english: But moving itself,
is it not because of carrying out?!
phrases.notes: The Sages forbade moving objects so that people would not come to carry them out.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְטִלְטוּל גּוּפֵיהּ לָאו מִשּׁוּם הוֹצָאָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the pushback of step 2 and saves the proof of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the two ideas are linked: טלטול is a rabbinic extension of הוצאה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: הוצאה and טלטול are separate, so a strict view on one says nothing about the other.
steps.terutzMaskana: טלטול is forbidden because of הוצאה, so being strict on הוצאה means being strict on טלטול.

steps.title: רב also agrees with רבא: the case of the hoe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רב holds like רבא. רב said that moving a hoe so it will not be stolen is forbidden טלטול שלא לצורך.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב also holds like this ruling of רבא. רב said: moving a hoe so that it will not be stolen is moving without a purpose, and it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a new support for רבא's ruling about moving objects, this time from a statement of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's ruling is that a tool whose main use is forbidden may be moved for its own use or for its spot, but not just to protect it. רב rules that moving a hoe only to keep it from being stolen counts as טלטול שלא לצורך and is forbidden. A hoe is used for digging, so it is a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור.

keyTerms.meaning: so that it will not be stolen
not for a purpose (not for using the object or its spot)

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף רַב סָבַר לַהּ לְהָא דְּרָבָא.
phrases.english: And even Rav holds like this ruling of Rava.
As Rav said:
A hoe, moved so that it will not be stolen,
this is moving without a purpose, and it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף רַב סָבַר לַהּ לְהָא דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new support for רבא's ruling, this time from רב.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור may be moved לצורך גופו and לצורך מקומו, but not just to protect it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's statement about the hoe moved so that it will not be stolen.

steps.title: Reading רב's words: use of the object or its spot is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws an inference from רב. The only reason moving the hoe is forbidden is that it was moved for protection. Moving it לצורך גופו or לצורך מקומו would be allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason it is forbidden is that it was moved so it would not be stolen. But for the use of the object itself, or for the use of its spot, it is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads closely into רב's words and shows how they match רבא exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב forbade only one specific case: moving for protection. That implies the other cases are allowed, namely moving the hoe to use it or to free up its space. This is exactly רבא's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: the reason is (often used to draw an inference)
for the use of the object itself
for the use of its spot (to free up the space)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, and here also רב, a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור may be moved for two reasons: to use it (לצורך גופו) or to use its spot (לצורך מקומו). Moving it just to protect it is forbidden.

phrases.english: The reason is that it was moved so it would not be stolen,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לְצוֹרֶךְ גּוּפוֹ וּלְצוֹרֶךְ מְקוֹמוֹ — מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: but for the use of the object itself or the use of its spot, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the implication from רב's statement in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That רב permits moving לצורך גופו and לצורך מקומו, just like רבא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The precise wording of רב's statement about the hoe.

steps.title: Challenge: רב had a net brought for רב כהנא to sit on
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether רב really holds this way. It brings a story: when רב כהנא visited, רב said to bring a net for him to sit on.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so?! But רב כהנא happened to come to רב's house, and רב said: bring a net for כהנא to sit on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a challenge against step 5 by telling a story about רב. This step sets up the problem, and the next step explains what bothers the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fishing net is used for trapping fish, which is a forbidden מלאכה. So it is a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור. רב allowed it to be moved so someone could sit on it, which is using the object itself.

keyTerms.meaning: but look, didn't... (brings a contradicting source)
a net, used for fishing or trapping
so he can sit on it

phrases.english: Is that so?! But Rav Kahana
happened to come to the house of Rav,
and Rav said: Bring him a net,
for Kahana, so he can sit on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי?! וְהָא רַב כָּהֲנָא אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference of step 5 with a story about רב himself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 5 that רב permits moving a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור even לצורך מקומו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב's own conduct with the net is used to show what he really holds. The next step spells out the inference.

steps.title: The inference: use of the object yes, its spot no
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the challenge. The story seems to teach that a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור may be moved לצורך גופו, but not לצורך מקומו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't this mean that a tool whose main use is forbidden may be moved for its own use, yes, but for its spot, no?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out what the story implies. This directly contradicts what it just read into רב's words about the hoe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא reads the story as pointing out a limit: רב allowed the net to be moved only because it would be used, for sitting. That suggests moving it only to clear its spot would be forbidden. This clashes with step 5, where רב seemed to allow both גופו and מקומו.

keyTerms.meaning: does this not mean to say? (draws an implication)
an object whose main use is forbidden on שבת (מוקצה מחמת איסור)

steps.confusionAlert: The net is still a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור. Sitting on it does not change that category. The question is only which uses are enough to allow moving it.

phrases.english: Is that not to say
that an object whose main function is forbidden,
for the use of the object itself, yes, it may be moved,
for the use of its spot, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge of step 6 by stating the implication that contradicts step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference in step 5 that רב permits moving לצורך מקומו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב's story implies only לצורך גופו is allowed. That contradicts the inference from his ruling on the hoe that לצורך מקומו is also allowed.

steps.title: What רב really said: remove the net from before כהנא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the story. What רב actually said was 'remove the net from in front of כהנא,' meaning clear the spot so he could sit there. That is moving it לצורך מקומו, which fits רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he said to them: Take the net away from in front of כהנא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 7 by correcting the story. רב did not say 'bring a net for כהנא to sit on.' What he really said was 'remove the net from in front of כהנא.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge depended on the wording 'bring it so he can sit on it,' which sounded like only לצורך גופו was allowed. The גמרא says that was not רב's real wording. He had the net removed so כהנא could use the spot, which is לצורך מקומו. So the story actually supports רבא's view that moving for the spot is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: a net (a fishing net, a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור)
this is what he really said to them

phrases.english: This is what he said to them:
phrases.notes: Introduces a corrected version of רב's words, replacing the earlier quote.

phrases.english: Remove the net from before Kahana.
phrases.notes: Moving it to clear the space = לצורך מקומו.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the report of the story: רב's actual words were different (remove the net, not bring it to sit on).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב only allowed moving the net to sit on it (לצורך גופו).
steps.terutzMaskana: רב actually had the net moved to clear the space (לצורך מקומו), so the story matches רבא.

steps.title: Second answer: the net was in the sun
steps.stepSummary: Another answer: the net was lying in the sun. רב's words only rule out moving it to protect it (מחמה לצל), not moving it for its space.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: there, it was a case of moving it from the sun to the shade.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to answer the question. The net was sitting in the sun, where it could get ruined.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב stressed 'to sit on' so that no one would think the net was being moved just to protect it from the sun, which is forbidden. So the inference 'only for sitting' rules out מחמה לצל, not לצורך מקומו.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you want, say (introduces another answer)
from the sun to the shade (moving an object only to protect it)

steps.confusionAlert: This second answer does not say רב forbids moving for space. It only says the point of רב's wording was to exclude moving to protect the object.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
There, it was a case of from the sun to the shade.
phrases.notes: The net was in a place where the sun could damage it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate answer to the same קשיא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining what the story's wording was meant to exclude.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'For sitting' means only לצורך גופו, so לצורך מקומו is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'For sitting' was said to rule out מחמה לצל, so רב still holds like רבא.

steps.title: רב מרי asks רבא about cushions in the sun
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי בר רחל had felt cushions lying in the sun on שבת. He asked רבא whether he may move them, and רבא said yes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי בר רחל had felt cushions lying in the sun. He came to רבא and asked: May I move them? רבא told him: It is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story about moving objects out of the sun. This sets up a back-and-forth that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cushions are a כלי שמלאכתו להיתר, an object normally used for permitted things. רבא at first permits moving them simply.

phrases.english: Rav Mari bar Raḥel

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה לֵיהּ הָהוּא בֵּי סַדְיְוָתָא בְּשִׁמְשָׁא.
phrases.english: had some felt cushions in the sun.
He came before Rava,
he said to him: What is the law about moving them?
He said to him: It is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב מָרִי בַּר רָחֵל הֲוָה לֵיהּ הָהוּא בֵּי סַדְיְוָתָא בְּשִׁמְשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story on the topic of moving things out of the sun.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא rules that moving the cushions is allowed.

steps.title: רב מרי says he does not need these cushions
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי says he has other cushions, and also others for guests. So his only reason to move these is to protect them.
steps.simpleTranslation: I have others. They are fit for guests. I also have others for guests.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי pushes back on רבא's permission. Each time רבא offers a use for the cushions, רב מרי shows he does not need them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא tried to make this a case of לצורך גופו (they could be used for guests). רב מרי removes that reason. That leaves a pure case of מחמה לצל, moving them only so the sun will not ruin them.

phrases.english: I have others.
phrases.notes: רב מרי speaking.

phrases.english: They are fit for guests.
phrases.notes: רבא speaking.

phrases.english: I also have others for guests.
phrases.notes: רב מרי speaking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the case from Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's permission to move the cushions.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is no real use for these cushions, so moving them is only to protect them (מחמה לצל).

steps.title: רבא: since you hold like רבה, it is forbidden for you
steps.stepSummary: רבא says: You show that you hold like רבה. For everyone else it is allowed, but for you it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You have shown that you hold like רבה. For everyone it is allowed; for you it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא ends the story with a ruling. רב מרי's own questions show he follows רבה's stricter view, so he must act on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By רבא's view, a כלי שמלאכתו להיתר may be moved even מחמה לצל, so everyone may move the cushions. רבה forbids this. Since רב מרי treats it as a problem, he holds like רבה, and he may not permit for himself what he thinks is forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: By רבא, a כלי שמלאכתו להיתר may be moved even מחמה לצל. But someone who holds the stricter view of רבה must keep it himself.

phrases.english: He said to him: You have revealed your opinion
that you hold like Rabba.
For everyone it is permitted,
for you it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the back-and-forth of Step 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Moving the cushions מחמה לצל is allowed in general (רבא), but forbidden for one who holds like רבה.

steps.title: רב: wool brooms may be moved, palm brooms may not
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that brooms of fine wool may be moved on שבת, but brooms of palm fronds may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said in the name of רבי חייא בר אשי in the name of רב: Brooms of fine wool may be moved on שבת, but those of palm fronds may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling of רב about brooms. It will soon use this ruling to test רב's view again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wool broom is gentle, so using it is permitted, which makes it a כלי שמלאכתו להיתר. A palm broom is a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור, because sweeping with it on שבת is forbidden (it can end up filling in holes in the floor). So רב forbids moving it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said that Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Ashi said that Rav said:
Brooms of fine wool —
it is permitted to move them on Shabbat,
but those of date palm — no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New ruling of רב, connected to the question of how רב holds.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wool brooms may be moved; palm brooms may not.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: even palm brooms may be moved
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר disagrees with רב and permits moving even palm-frond brooms.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: Even those of palm fronds may be moved.
steps.whatsHappening: As the text first reads, רבי אלעזר argues on רב. This sets up the גמרא's question about what case they are talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב forbids the palm broom and רבי אלעזר permits it. The גמרא now needs to find a case where this argument makes sense.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: אַף שֶׁל תְּמָרָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says: Even those of date palm.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: אַף שֶׁל תְּמָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Appears to argue with רב in Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Palm brooms may also be moved.

steps.title: Which case? Not for its use or its space
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case this is. It cannot be moving the broom for its use or its space, since רב holds like רבא, who allows that.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with? If you say it is for the object's own use and for its space, would רב say palm brooms are forbidden? But רב holds like רבא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what case רב and רבי אלעזר are arguing about. It tries the first option and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A palm broom is a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור. רבא allows moving such an object לצורך גופו ולצורך מקומו, and we already proved (Step 4) that רב holds like רבא. So רב could not forbid moving it in that case.

keyTerms.meaning: what case are we dealing with?
to use the space it takes up

phrases.english: With what are we dealing?
If you say for the purpose of itself and for the purpose of its place —

phrases.aramaic: בְּהָא לֵימָא רַב שֶׁל תְּמָרָה לָא?
phrases.english: in this case would Rav say that those of date palm are not allowed?
But Rav holds like Rava!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the case behind Steps 13–14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which kind of moving are רב and רבי אלעזר arguing about?
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading רב's ruling as about לצורך גופו ומקומו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב holds like רבא, who permits that kind of moving.

steps.title: If it is from sun to shade, how can רבי אלעזר permit?
steps.stepSummary: So the case must be moving the broom מחמה לצל. But then how can רבי אלעזר allow it?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is from the sun to the shade. But in that case, would רבי אלעזר say even palm brooms are allowed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the second option, מחמה לצל. That fits רב well, but now רבי אלעזר's view is hard to understand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moving a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור just to protect it is forbidden according to everyone. So רב's ban makes sense, but רבי אלעזר's permission does not.

keyTerms.meaning: in this case would he say?

phrases.english: Rather, from the sun to the shade:

phrases.aramaic: בְּהָא לֵימָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אַף שֶׁל תְּמָרָה?
phrases.english: In this case would Rabbi Elazar say even those of date palm?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the first option, attacks the second option.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Moving a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור only to protect it should be forbidden, so רבי אלעזר could not permit it.

steps.title: Fix the text: רבי אלעזר agrees with רב
steps.stepSummary: The case really is מחמה לצל, and the text should read: 'And so said רבי אלעזר.' He agrees with רב that it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it is from the sun to the shade. Change the text and say: 'And so too said רבי אלעזר.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing the wording. רבי אלעזר did not argue on רב; he said the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the case is מחמה לצל, a palm broom may not be moved, and both רב and רבי אלעזר agree. This also confirms again that רב holds like רבא.
steps.whatToRemember: Palm brooms (a כלי שמלאכתו לאיסור) may not be moved מחמה לצל. רב and רבי אלעזר agree, which fits רב holding like רבא.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'אף של תמרה' as a real argument. The גמרא changes the text so that רבי אלעזר agrees with רב.

phrases.english: Actually, from the sun to the shade,
say: And so too said Rabbi Elazar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the text (from an argument to agreement).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר argues on רב and permits palm brooms.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אלעזר agrees with רב: palm brooms may not be moved מחמה לצל.

steps.title: Broken pieces may be moved if they are still useful
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that shards of movable כלים may be moved on שבת if they can do some useful job. It gives examples: covering a barrel or a jug.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Any כלי that may be moved on שבת, its broken pieces may also be moved, as long as the pieces can still do some kind of useful job. For example, pieces of a big bowl can cover the mouth of a barrel, and pieces of glass can cover the mouth of a small jug.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives the basic rule (the view of the תנא קמא) about moving broken pieces of כלים on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Broken pieces might seem like junk, and junk is normally מוקצה. The משנה says they keep their permitted status as long as they can still be used for something. According to this first opinion, the use does not need to match what the כלי originally did. A bowl shard can be used as a lid.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; the start of a new משנה
May be moved or carried around (on שבת)
Broken pieces, shards / their broken pieces
Fit for some kind of useful job (any use)
A large bowl or trough, such as a kneading bowl

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic test for shards: being useful is what keeps them from becoming מוקצה. The rest of the sugya argues over how close that use must be to the original use.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
phrases.notes: A new משנה begins here.

phrases.english: All vessels that may be moved on Shabbat —
their shards may be moved along with them,
phrases.notes: The pieces share the permitted status of the whole כלי.

phrases.english: as long as they are suited for some purpose.
phrases.notes: Any useful purpose is enough.

phrases.aramaic: שִׁבְרֵי עֲרֵיבָה לְכַסּוֹת בָּהֶן אֶת פִּי הֶחָבִית,
phrases.english: Shards of a large bowl — to cover the mouth of a barrel with them,
phrases.notes: A bowl was never a lid, but this new use still counts.

phrases.aramaic: שִׁבְרֵי זְכוּכִית לְכַסּוֹת בָּהֶן אֶת פִּי הַפַּךְ.
phrases.english: shards of glass — to cover the mouth of a cruse with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַכֵּלִים הַנִּיטָּלִין בַּשַּׁבָּת שִׁבְרֵיהֶן נִיטָּלִין עִמָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה. It continues the general theme of moving כלים on שבת, now applied to broken כלים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Shards of movable כלים may be moved on שבת if they are fit for any useful purpose, even a purpose different from the original one.

steps.title: רבי יהודה requires a use similar to the original
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the shards may be moved only if they can still do a job like the one the כלי originally did.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Only if the pieces can still do something similar to their original job. Bowl pieces must still be able to hold soup poured into them, and glass pieces must still be able to hold oil poured into them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the first opinion and sets a stricter test for moving shards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, any use is enough. For רבי יהודה, the shard must still work roughly like the original כלי. A bowl shard that can only serve as a lid is not enough for him. It must still be able to hold food.
steps.confusionAlert: Watch for the small difference in wording. The תנא קמא says מְלָאכָה (any job), while רבי יהודה says מְלַאכְתָּן (THEIR job, meaning the original one). The whole מחלוקת depends on that word.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Only as long as they are suited for a purpose similar to their original use:
phrases.notes: This is stricter than the תנא קמא.

phrases.english: shards of a large bowl — fit to pour soup into them,
phrases.notes: They still act as a container for food, as the bowl did.

phrases.english: and those of glass — fit to pour oil into them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר בִּלְבַד שֶׁיְּהוּ עוֹשִׂין מֵעֵין מְלַאכְתָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the תנא קמא of Step 18 by narrowing which uses count.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Shards may be moved only if they are fit for a use similar to the original function of the כלי.

steps.title: שמואל: the argument is only about כלים broken before שבת
steps.stepSummary: שמואל limits the מחלוקת of the משנה to כלים that broke on ערב שבת. He then explains each side: רבי יהודה needs a similar use, while the חכמים accept any use.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The argument is only about pieces that broke before שבת began. One Sage (רבי יהודה) holds that a similar use is allowed and a different use is not. The other Sage (the חכמים) holds that even a different use is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with שמואל, who tells us when the משנה's argument applies: only when the כלי broke on ערב שבת. He then restates both opinions in that case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל adds new information that the משנה never stated: the timing of the break. When the כלי broke before שבת, the pieces start שבת already as shards, so we must judge whether they count as a usable item. By limiting the argument to this case, שמואל hints that a break on שבת itself may be judged differently, and the גמרא will deal with that next.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion that analyzes the משנה
A dispute; here, it limits where the argument applies
One Sage holds … and the other Sage holds

steps.whatToRemember: According to שמואל, the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה argue only about כלים that broke before שבת. רבי יהודה needs a use like the original one, and the חכמים accept any useful purpose.
steps.whyThisMatters: By limiting the argument to breaks before שבת, שמואל sets up the next question in the גמרא: what is the law when the כלי breaks on שבת itself?

phrases.english: GEMARA:
phrases.notes: The גמרא's discussion of the משנה begins.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
phrases.notes: Attribution line, merged into the statement it introduces.

phrases.english: The dispute is where they broke on Shabbat eve,
phrases.notes: This limits the case. It is not stated in the משנה.

phrases.english: for one Sage (Rabbi Yehuda) holds: a purpose similar to their original use — yes,
a purpose of some other use — no.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: אֲפִילּוּ מֵעֵין מְלָאכָה אַחֶרֶת.
phrases.english: And the other Sage (the Rabbis) holds: even for some other use.
phrases.notes: The תנא קמא of the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל מַחֲלוֹקֶת שֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרוּ מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Interprets the מחלוקת of Steps 18–19 by defining the case it applies to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מחלוקת between the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה applies only to כלים broken on ערב שבת. In that case, רבי יהודה permits only a similar use, and the חכמים permit even a different use.

steps.title: שמואל: Shards broken on שבת are permitted by everyone
steps.stepSummary: The end of the first version of שמואל's statement: if the כלים broke on שבת itself, everyone agrees the shards may be moved, because they were already 'prepared' through the whole כלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if they broke on שבת, everyone agrees they are permitted. Since they were 'prepared' through their 'parent' (the original כלי), it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes שמואל's statement from step 20. He adds that shards from a כלי that broke on שבת itself may be moved according to everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the start of שבת, the whole כלי was ready for use, so it was not מוקצה. שמואל holds that the shards take on that status from their 'parent' כלי, so they count as already prepared. This is why even רבי יהודה would allow them in this case.

keyTerms.meaning: Prepared (ready for use from before שבת, so not מוקצה)
By virtue of their 'parent': the original whole כלי

steps.confusionAlert: This is only the FIRST version of שמואל's statement. In step 24 the גמרא will replace it with a version that flips which case is disputed.

phrases.english: But if they broke on Shabbat
everyone agrees they are permitted.

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וּמוּכָנִין עַל גַּבֵּי אֲבִיהֶן — מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: Since they are prepared through their 'parents' (the original vessels), it is permitted.
phrases.notes: The whole כלי was usable when שבת began, so its pieces share that 'prepared' status.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes שמואל's statement from step 20 by ruling on the case of כלים that broke on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Shards of כלים that broke on שבת may be moved by everyone, because they are prepared through the original כלי.

steps.title: רב זוטרא cites a ברייתא: burn whole vessels, not shards
steps.stepSummary: רב זוטרא challenges שמואל with a ברייתא: on יום טוב you may burn whole כלים as fuel, but not shards of כלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זוטרא raised an objection: We may light a fire with כלים, but we may not light a fire with shards of כלים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זוטרא brings a ברייתא to challenge שמואל. This step only quotes the source. The next step explains why it contradicts שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is about fuel on יום טוב. Whole כלים are allowed, but shards are forbidden, so shards are treated as more restricted. This hints that shards can be a 'new thing' that is not prepared, which goes against step 21.

keyTerms.meaning: Raised an objection (usually from a ברייתא or משנה)
We light / use as fuel for a fire
A Festival day, when cooking and lighting fires is allowed but מוקצה rules still apply

phrases.english: Rav Zutra raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: מַסִּיקִין בְּכֵלִים, וְאֵין מַסִּיקִין בְּשִׁבְרֵי כֵלִים.
phrases.english: One may kindle (a fire on a Festival) with vessels, but one may not kindle with shards of vessels.
phrases.notes: A ברייתא about which items may be burned as fuel on יום טוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks שמואל's ruling from step 21 using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that shards broken on שבת are permitted by everyone (step 21).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids shards while permitting whole כלים, which suggests freshly broken shards are a forbidden 'new thing' and are not prepared through the original כלי.

steps.title: Proving the ברייתא means shards broken on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks when the shards in the ברייתא broke. Before יום טוב makes no sense, because then they are just wood. So it must mean they broke on יום טוב, and the ברייתא forbids them, against שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: When did they break? If you say they broke before יום טוב, they are simply wood! So it must be that they broke on יום טוב, and it teaches: we may light with כלים but not with shards of כלים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens רב זוטרא's challenge by proving which case the ברייתא is talking about. Once it is clear the shards broke on יום טוב, the contradiction with שמואל is complete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Shards that broke before יום טוב are just ordinary firewood, so there is no reason to forbid burning them. The only sensible reading is that they broke on יום טוב itself, and the ברייתא forbids them. That is the opposite of שמואל, who said shards that broke on the holy day are permitted by everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a reading that will be rejected)
Rather, is it not (introduces the forced reading)

phrases.english: (Vessels) that broke when?
If you say that they broke before the Festival?
They are just ordinary wood!
phrases.notes: So there would be no reason to forbid burning them.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not (that they broke) on the Festival,
and it teaches: One may kindle with vessels
but one may not kindle with shards of vessels!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains step 22 by pinning down the case of the ברייתא, which completes the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that shards broken on the holy day itself are permitted by everyone.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Shards broken before יום טוב are just wood, so the ברייתא must mean shards broken on יום טוב. It forbids those, which shows that freshly broken shards are not automatically 'prepared.'

steps.title: A new version of שמואל: the dispute is about shards broken on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewrites שמואל's statement. The מחלוקת is about shards that broke on שבת: the חכמים say they are מוכן, while רבי יהודה says they are נולד. Shards that broke before שבת are permitted by everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The מחלוקת is when they broke on שבת. One master holds it is מוכן, and the other master holds it is נולד. But if they broke before שבת, everyone agrees they are permitted, since they were prepared for some use while it was still day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב זוטרא by replacing the first version of שמואל's statement with a new one. This new version fits the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the case of shards broken on the holy day is the disputed case. רבי יהודה treats them as נולד, a new thing that is forbidden, and the ברייתא can follow his view. The חכמים treat them as מוכן through the original כלי. Shards broken before שבת were already usable pieces when שבת began, so everyone permits them.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said, this is how it was said (the גמרא corrects an earlier version of a statement)
One master holds... and the other master holds
'Newly born': an item that came into existence on שבת or יום טוב and is forbidden as מוקצה
While it was still day (before שבת began)

steps.whatToRemember: Final version of שמואל: Shards broken before שבת are permitted by everyone. Shards broken on שבת are disputed: the חכמים say מוכן (permitted), and רבי יהודה says נולד (forbidden). The ברייתא about יום טוב fuel fits רבי יהודה.
steps.confusionAlert: The two versions flip the cases. First version: the dispute is about shards broken on ערב שבת, and shards broken on שבת are permitted by all. Final version: the dispute is about shards broken on שבת, and shards broken on ערב שבת are permitted by all. Also note which side is which: the חכמים say מוכן, and רבי יהודה says נולד.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the idea of נולד as a reason for מוקצה, which comes back many times in the laws of שבת and יום טוב.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was stated, it was stated like this:
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The dispute is where they broke on Shabbat,
for one master holds it is prepared,
phrases.notes: The חכמים: the pieces were prepared as part of the whole כלי.

phrases.english: and the other master holds it is a newly created thing,
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה: the shards are a new item that came into being on שבת.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת — דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל מוּתָּרִין,
phrases.english: but (if they broke) before Shabbat, everyone agrees they are permitted,
since they were prepared for a use while it was still day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 22-23 by rewriting שמואל's statement from steps 20-21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-versioning: the original report of the אמורא's statement is replaced with a corrected version.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל said the dispute is about shards broken on ערב שבת, and that everyone permits shards broken on שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל said the dispute is about shards broken on שבת (מוכן vs. נולד), and everyone permits shards broken on ערב שבת. The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה's view of נולד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Shards broken before שבת are permitted by everyone. Shards broken on שבת are disputed between the חכמים (מוכן) and רבי יהודה (נולד).

steps.title: Three teachings that disagree about burning כלים on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes three ברייתות about using כלים as fuel on יום טוב. One permits whole כלים but not shards, one permits both, and one forbids both.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא taught: you may burn whole כלים as fuel, but not shards of כלים. Another ברייתא taught: just as you may burn whole כלים, you may also burn shards. A third ברייתא taught: you may burn neither whole כלים nor shards.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists three ברייתות that seem to clash about what you may use as fuel on יום טוב. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא will explain each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא is the one רב זוטרא quoted earlier. Now we see two more ברייתות with opposite rulings: one says everything is allowed and one says nothing is allowed. Three different rulings on the same case need an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: We may kindle, meaning use something as fuel for a fire
Shards or broken pieces of כלים

phrases.english: One baraita taught:
phrases.notes: This is about יום טוב, when cooking fires are allowed.

phrases.english: One may kindle a fire with whole vessels,
but one may not kindle with shards of vessels.
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא רב זוטרא used against שמואל.

phrases.english: And another baraita taught:
Just as one may kindle with vessels,
so too one may kindle with shards of vessels.
And yet another baraita taught:
One may not kindle, neither with vessels
nor with shards of vessels.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי חֲדָא וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rewriting שמואל's statement, the גמרא brings the full set of ברייתות on this topic, including the one רב זוטרא quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The three ברייתות against each other
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same case, burning כלים and shards on יום טוב, gets three opposite rulings, so they cannot all follow one view.

steps.title: Each teaching follows a different תנא
steps.stepSummary: The first ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, the second follows רבי שמעון, and the third follows רבי נחמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא follows רבי יהודה. That ברייתא follows רבי שמעון. And this one follows רבי נחמיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by saying each ברייתא follows a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that something newly formed on יום טוב is forbidden. Shards that broke on יום טוב are new, so they are forbidden, while whole כלים are fine. רבי שמעון does not have this rule, so he permits both. רבי נחמיה allows using a כלי only for its normal job, and burning is not a normal job, so he forbids both.

keyTerms.meaning: This one... that one. Used to assign different sources to different opinions
Something newly formed on שבת or יום טוב, which רבי יהודה forbids
A תנא who allows moving a כלי only for its intended use

steps.whatToRemember: Three ברייתות, three views: רבי יהודה forbids only shards (they are נולד), רבי שמעון permits both, and רבי נחמיה forbids both.
steps.whyThisMatters: This fits the rewritten version of שמואל. Shards that broke on the holy day itself are exactly what רבי יהודה forbids as נולד.

phrases.english: This one is Rabbi Yehuda.
phrases.notes: Whole כלים are allowed. Shards that broke on יום טוב are נולד.

phrases.english: That one is Rabbi Shimon.
phrases.notes: There is no מוקצה or נולד rule here, so both are allowed.

phrases.english: This one is Rabbi Neḥemya.
phrases.notes: A כלי may be used only for its normal purpose, so both are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הָא רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each source to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The three ברייתות seemed to give opposite rulings on one law.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each ברייתא reflects the view of a different תנא, so there is no real contradiction.

steps.title: Leftover bricks may be moved unless they were stacked
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that bricks left over from building may be moved on שבת because people sit on them. Once they are stacked in a pile, they are clearly set aside and become מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: bricks left over from a building may be moved, because they are fit to sit on. If someone stacked them up, he certainly set them aside, and they may not be moved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: a ruling from רב נחמן about moving leftover building bricks on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the building is finished, the extra bricks have a new use as seats, so they are not מוקצה. But stacking them in a neat pile shows the owner is saving them for future building. That decision sets them aside, and moving them becomes forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: He set them aside, making them מוקצה

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the same object can be allowed or forbidden depending on what the owner's actions show about his plans for it.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said:
These bricks that were left over from the building:
it is permitted to move them,
because they are fit to sit on.
If he stacked them, he certainly set them aside.
phrases.notes: Stacking shows he is saving them for building, so they become מוקצה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן הָנֵי לִיבְנֵי דְּאִישְׁתַּיּוּר מִבִּנְיָינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new but related מוקצה question: leftover building materials.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leftover bricks may be moved because people sit on them, unless they were stacked away, which makes them מוקצה.

steps.title: שמואל: a small shard may be moved in a courtyard only
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן quotes שמואל: a small earthenware shard may be moved in a חצר, but not in a כרמלית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: a small earthenware shard may be moved in a courtyard, but not in a כרמלית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling from שמואל about moving a small piece of broken earthenware on שבת. This opens a short disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A small shard counts as useful only where there is something to use it for. In a חצר there are כלים around that it can cover, so it may be moved there. In a כרמלית there are usually no such כלים, so it has no use and stays forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A small piece of broken earthenware
A courtyard, a private area people use
A semi-public area, neither fully private nor fully public, forbidden by רבנן for carrying

steps.confusionAlert: This argument is about מוקצה: is the shard useful enough to move? It is not about the laws of carrying between domains. The place matters only because it decides whether the shard has a use there.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said that Shmuel said:
A small earthenware shard:
it is permitted to move it in a courtyard,
phrases.notes: There are כלים there that it can cover.

phrases.english: but in a karmelit, no.
phrases.notes: There it usually has no use.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל חֶרֶס קְטַנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another ruling from רב נחמן about moving broken or leftover items.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A small shard may be moved in a חצר, where it is useful, but not in a כרמלית.

steps.title: רב נחמן: even in a כרמלית, but not in the public domain
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, in his own name, goes further than שמואל: the shard may be moved even in a כרמלית, but not in רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן himself said: even in a כרמלית it may be moved, but in רשות הרבים it may not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives his own opinion, which is more lenient than the one he quoted from שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן sees enough use for the shard even in a כרמלית, so he widens the permission one step. He still draws the line at רשות הרבים, where he holds the shard has no real use.

keyTerms.meaning: His own, meaning his own opinion

phrases.english: And Rav Naḥman himself said:
Even in a karmelit it is permitted,
but in the public domain, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב נַחְמָן דִּידֵיהּ אָמַר אֲפִילּוּ בְּכַרְמְלִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with שמואל's view from Step 28 and is more lenient.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A small shard may be moved even in a כרמלית, but not in רשות הרבים.

steps.title: רבא: even in the public domain
steps.stepSummary: רבא is the most lenient: a small shard may be moved even in רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: even in רשות הרבים it may be moved.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the most lenient view in the disagreement: the shard may be moved anywhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא holds that a small shard is useful even in the public domain, so it is never מוקצה. Now we have three levels: שמואל allows a חצר only, רב נחמן adds a כרמלית, and רבא adds רשות הרבים.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who here gives the most lenient view

steps.whatToRemember: A small shard: שמואל allows moving it only in a חצר, רב נחמן also allows it in a כרמלית, and רבא allows it even in רשות הרבים.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
Even in the public domain it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes further than רב נחמן's view in Step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A small shard may be moved even in רשות הרבים.

steps.title: רבא's servant wipes his shoe with a street shard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבא acts on his own ruling. His servant picked up a shard in the street of מחוזא to wipe clay off רבא's shoe, and the רבנן protested.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא follows his own reasoning. רבא was once walking in the street of מחוזא, and his shoes got dirty with clay. His servant came, took a shard of earthenware, and wiped the clay off. The Sages raised their voices at him in protest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story to show that רבא really lived by his lenient ruling from Step 30. It also sets up רבא's defense in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 30, רבא said a small shard may be moved even in רשות הרבים. Here a shard is picked up in a public street and used on שבת, which is exactly that case in real life. The רבנן's protest shows that others held the stricter views of שמואל or רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: He follows his own reasoning (he acts consistently with his stated view)
They raised their voice at him (a rebuke)

phrases.english: And Rava follows his own reasoning.
phrases.notes: This connects back to רבא's ruling in Step 30.

phrases.english: For Rava was walking
in the street of Meḥoza,
phrases.notes: A public street, so it counts as רשות הרבים.

phrases.english: his shoes became dirty with clay.
His servant came,
took a shard and wiped it off.
The Sages raised their voice at him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This story shows רבא's ruling from Step 30 being put into practice.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that a small shard may be moved even in רשות הרבים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבא's servant using a street shard in מחוזא

steps.title: רבא defends using the shard
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers the protest. In a חצר, the shard would be useful for covering a vessel. So here too it is useful, for wiping his shoe.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Is it not enough that they did not learn, but they also teach others? If the shard were in a courtyard, wouldn't it be fit to cover a vessel with it? Here too, it is fit for my use.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא responds to the רבנן and explains why moving the shard was permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's logic is that the shard's usefulness does not change based on where it lies. Everyone agrees it is useful, and so movable, in a חצר. In the street it has a real use too, like wiping a shoe, so it is not מוקצה there either.

keyTerms.meaning: It is fit or suitable for use

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the key test for whether an object is מוקצה: is it fit for some use? Location alone does not decide it.

phrases.english: He said: Is it not enough that they did not learn,
but they also teach others?!
If it were in a courtyard,
would it not be fit
to cover a vessel with it?
Here too, it is fit for me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the רבנן's protest from Step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical comparison: if the shard is useful in a חצר, it is useful in the street too
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן thought a shard in רשות הרבים may not be moved
steps.terutzMaskana: The shard is fit for use anywhere, so it may be moved even in רשות הרבים

steps.title: A broken jug seal may be moved on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: a clay seal of a jug that broke may still be moved on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the clay seal of a jug that broke may be moved on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling about another broken clay object: the seal of a jug.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the seal can no longer do its original job, it is not considered junk. Its pieces still have uses, so they do not become מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: The clay seal or stopper of a jug
To move or carry (within the permitted area)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The seal of a jug that was broken —
it is permitted to move on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This moves from shards in general to a related case, a broken jug seal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A broken jug seal may be moved on שבת.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports שמואל and adds limits
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא agrees that a broken seal and its pieces may be moved. It adds two limits: you may not break off a piece for use, and if the seal was thrown into the garbage it becomes forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: A seal that broke, it and its pieces may be moved on שבת. But one may not break off a piece from it to cover a vessel or to prop up the legs of a bed. And if he threw it into the garbage dump, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports שמואל's ruling. The ברייתא also adds two restrictions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא matches שמואל: the broken seal and its pieces are movable. Breaking off a new piece is forbidden because it is like making a new utensil on שבת. Throwing the seal into the garbage shows the owner has given up on it, so it becomes מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא supports the ruling)

steps.confusionAlert: Moving the broken pieces is permitted, but breaking off a new piece is forbidden. These are two different acts.

phrases.english: It was also taught so:
A seal that was broken —
it and its shards may be moved on Shabbat.
But one may not break off a shard from it
to cover a vessel with it
or to support the legs of a bed with it.
And if he threw it into the garbage dump — it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: Throwing it away shows the owner gave up on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This supports שמואל's ruling with a ברייתא and adds limits to it.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that a broken seal may be moved
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a broken מגופה

steps.title: רב פפא challenges the garbage-dump rule
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא objects: if throwing something into the garbage makes it forbidden, then a cloak thrown there should also be forbidden. That is clearly wrong. He then begins his own explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא challenged this: If so, if someone throws his cloak into the garbage, would that also be forbidden?! Rather, רב פפא said:
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks the ברייתא's rule that throwing an object into the garbage makes it forbidden. He then sets up his own alternative reading, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A cloak is still a perfectly good garment even if someone tossed it onto the garbage. So simply throwing something away cannot by itself make it מוקצה. The ending words 'אלא אמר רב פפא' show that he is about to give a different explanation of the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, then (introducing an absurd result)

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not arguing with the main ruling that the broken seal may be moved. He is only challenging why throwing it into the garbage would make it forbidden.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa strongly objects to it:
If that is so,
if one throws his cloak there,
would it also be forbidden?!
Rather, Rav Pappa said:
phrases.notes: This sets up רב פפא's own explanation, which continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This challenges the last clause of the ברייתא in Step 34.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that a seal thrown into the garbage becomes forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By that logic, a cloak thrown into the garbage would also be forbidden. That is absurd, since a cloak is still clearly useful.
